faq: What is an AI model inventory?
A current list of the AI models your business uses, in your products, your systems and your suppliers' services, with where each runs, who owns it and whether it is approved.
Is this the same as AI security posture management, shadow AI discovery or a CASB?
Those tools watch and control how AI is used. This answers a different question: which models are in use, and can you prove it. It can sit alongside them.
Why not just ask teams and suppliers?

You should, and we help you structure the questions. Answers from people are incomplete and go out of date quickly, and a questionnaire is not evidence. The inventory gives you something to check them against.
Does it find shadow AI?
It looks for AI use that is not on your approved list, across the areas we agree in scope, and says what it could not see.
Does it cover AI inside our suppliers' products?
Where it shows up in your own estate and with the supplier's help. Where it cannot be confirmed, the report marks it open and suggests the question to put to the supplier.
Do you need agents on our endpoints or changes to our network?
We agree what access is needed before we start. We aim to work from what you already have, with read-only access, and we do not sit in the path of your live traffic.
Does it read our prompts or customer data?
No. It does not need to.
Can it show open models running on our own GPUs?
Yes, if you want that in scope.
Does it help with ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act or customer questionnaires?
It gives you the factual inventory those frameworks and questionnaires ask for. It does not certify compliance and it is not legal advice.
Which models can it flag, for example DeepSeek?
Whichever your policy rules out. Governments and customers have started naming particular models, and we flag whatever you list.
Is the report a certificate?
No. It is an attestation report that states its scope and date and says what we found in that scope. It does not claim to prove that nothing ruled out exists anywhere in your company.
How do we know the answer is complete?
The report says what was covered, what was not and our confidence in each finding. Where it is partial, we tell you, and we tell you what would close the gap.
Do UK firms have to keep an AI model inventory?

Not by a single UK rule that we can point to. Customers, suppliers and risk teams are asking the question, and frameworks such as ISO 42001 expect a register of AI in use. We will tell you if you do not need it.
How long does it take, and what does it cost?
We scope it with you first, agree a first milestone, then quote.

tiers: For the CIO, head of IT operations, procurement and finance. Discovery, spend and contract matching, the front door, fulfilment and seat pool, renewals, licence reclamation, offboarding, access reviews, the savings ledger and the IT pack. It also includes a read API, a read-only MCP server and continuous export to a bucket you own.

For the head of architecture. Capability mapping, TIME assessment, technology risk and standards, tiered architecture reviews, the decision log, derived lifecycle, observed interfaces, the rationalisation workbench, the roadmap and the architecture pack.

details_lead: Twenty-eight smaller features sit around the ten above, grouped by the loop. Each says what it does and how it behaves when it runs.

details.name: Discover
items: On the first sighting of an unapproved app, the product scores its risk, checks for overlap and asks the first user what it is for and what data goes in. A free, low-risk app with five users or fewer and no overlap is marked Allowed. Overlap triggers an offer of the approved app. Blocking is advisory, and revoking access is always a ticket.

Card descriptors and invoices are cleaned and matched to vendors, invoices are split by line, and currency is converted at the transaction-date rate. Contract terms are extracted by AI and stay Inferred until a named person confirms them. The product never reads full card numbers and never makes payments.

Each application has a business, technical and budget owner. The product suggests an owner with the reason, such as "212 active users in Marketing, renews 14 March", and asks Accept, Not me or Ask a question. Leavers' apps move to their manager the same day, and nobody gets more than one question or nudge per app a week.

For custom, hosted and desktop software, the product joins versions to end-of-support dates and to your adopt, trial, contain and retire standards. The technical owner picks Plan upgrade, Accept risk until a date or Already handled. Accepted risk expires and re-triggers.
App-to-app OAuth grants, API connections and MCP links seen by the feeds are recorded as interfaces, so the impact of retiring an application shows what depends on it.

details.name: Decide
items: Access requests pick a tier, role and duration and follow the policy's approval chain. A pooled seat is used first, and the seat expires by ticket. Use is checked after 30 days. Purchases go in parallel to the budget owner, security, the architect and procurement, and the signed contract creates the vendor, application and renewal. Privileged roles never self-serve.

A daily digest proposes a route for each demand: fast track, one-screen case, full case, merge or reject with a reason. The demand manager accepts or changes it in one click. Findings and renewals never create initiatives on their own.

The product drafts options, cost lines and benefit lines, each bound to a measure such as "matched spend reaches zero". The project manager writes up to 300 words and a sponsor confirms. Above the board threshold, finance reviews and the portfolio board approves.

Initiatives are scored for strategic fit, financial return, cost removed, risk reduction and delivery confidence, ranked, and a funding line is drawn. Manual moves need a visible reason, and the board approves the funded list. Estimated effort is totalled by team per quarter.

Candidates are ranked by saving multiplied by confidence, with a target app. The impact view shows users, interfaces, data to export and the last safe notice day. On approval it raises a demand carrying the evidence, fast-tracked if small.

details.name: Change
items: Each gate pack marks every item evidenced, attested or missing. At the build gate the product checks that the review passed with no open conditions, that security and data protection are signed off and that a baseline exists. Variance opens a pre-filled change request, and impact changes reopen architecture review.

Schedule, cost, scope, adoption, risk and overdue conditions each get a rating from the data. The project manager gets a card to confirm, edit or override with a reason. After Friday noon an unconfirmed status is published marked "not confirmed by PM". Adoption turns red only on Likely or Confirmed usage.

The roadmap is derived from each initiative's impacts and milestones. The product detects conflicts such as a retirement after a notice date, a capability left with no Invest app, or two initiatives on one app in a quarter, and posts each to the risk log as a suggestion with evidence.

For each leaver the product computes their footprint, checks identity deactivation, raises one ticket per non-SSO account, returns licences to the pool and proposes ownership transfer to the manager. It also flags agents, keys and card subscriptions under the leaver's identity. It deactivates and never deletes, and a legal hold stops destructive steps.

A campaign recommends keep or revoke with a reason: leaver, unused for 90 days, policy deviation or moved. Reviewers act from a chat or email card without logging in. Leaver revocations are accepted automatically, privileged access needs a second reviewer, and there is no approve-all on it. The campaign closes with an evidence pack for auditors.

details.name: Prove
items: For each retired app the product checks zero assignments, no sign-ins for 30 days, unassigned licences, evidence of non-renewal and two billing cycles without spend. Nobody sets Retired by hand. The owner attests data archiving and retention, and benefits are handed over with 3, 6 and 12-month reviews.

The IT pack covers spend, savings, renewals, shadow AI and coverage. The architecture pack and the portfolio pack follow with their tiers. Each opens with the decisions needed, links every figure to evidence and carries an AI-drafted narrative labelled a draft until the author releases it. They share as a page without a login, with PDF and slide exports.
Read API, MCP server and continuous export

A read API and a read-only MCP server answer questions over your data, and any proposal they make needs a person to approve it. The full dataset exports continuously to a bucket you own, with a documented schema.
A one-off upload with column mapping brings in project registers, project plans and spreadsheets, so the portfolio starts with history. Imported rows are marked as imported.

After the first value report you can add a browser extension, device management and AI vendor usage reports. The product shows a scope manifest for each, and an aggregate-only mode and a works council pack are available for Europe.

Technology components for custom software are read from cloud accounts and code hosts, so the standards and obsolescence views stay current without manual entry.
Discovery for further agent and automation platforms, more procurement connectors, a planning-tool connector for status and a ticketing connector for incidents.
Where pilots ask for it and security teams accept it, access can be granted by adding a person to an allow-listed group instead of by ticket.

Opt-in, anonymised price benchmarks across customers, and a dashboard builder for views we have not thought of.

ai_lead: AI drafts, suggests and summarises inside each flow. It acts alone only on a reversible change to the product's own records, above a confidence threshold. A named person decides everything else, and every AI suggestion is labelled as one.

know_h: Good to know before you talk to us
know: This page describes a product being built. The status beside each feature is our current intention, not a delivery date, and it may change as design partners tell us what matters.
The product has a fixed set of workflows. You change thresholds, approvers, channels and exemptions in settings, preview the effect and dry-run any workflow, but there is no general workflow builder.
It uses a small, fixed data model with tags and a few custom fields per object. There is no configurable metamodel.
It is not a diagram tool. It does not model business processes or value streams, and it is not a scheduling, task or timesheet tool.
It does not scan mailboxes or calendars, inspect prompts, handle payments or virtual cards, or send anything to a vendor on your behalf.
It does not run on your own servers. It is delivered as a service.
faq: What is Arithim Estate?

A system of record for the technology a company runs, what it pays for, why it has it and what will change it. It combines SaaS management, enterprise architecture and portfolio management on one set of records, so the three views agree.
How do I find shadow AI in my company?

Connect read-only to your identity provider, finance and card feeds and the AI vendors' admin reports. Arithim Estate finds AI tools, assistants and agents that nobody registered, shows who uses them, what they cost and what data they can reach, and asks the owner to confirm. It records metadata only and never reads prompts or outputs.
Does it help with AI governance and the EU AI Act?

It gives you the inventory and the owner, risk tier and review records those programmes start from. It is not legal advice. If you also need dated proof of which AI models you depend on, pair it with the AI model inventory.
Is it SaaS management, enterprise architecture or PMO software?

All three, on the same data. The SaaS management core is always included. The architecture and portfolio tiers add capability mapping, reviews and decisions on one side and demand, cases, gates and benefits on the other.
How long until I see value?

The first report arrives within ten working days of connecting read-only to your identity provider, finance export, card feed and contracts. It shows spend, unused seats, shadow IT and shadow AI, and renewals by notice date.
Does it change anything in our systems?

In the first release it writes messages in Slack, Teams and email, tickets in one queue you name and, if you switch it on, epics in one delivery project. With your second consent it can also remove people from allow-listed licence groups after 30 days in review-only mode. It never writes to finance, ERP or HR systems.
Can we start with only the SaaS management core?
Yes. You still get the front door, the seat pool, the renewal clock, licence reclamation and the savings ledger. Requests that need a bigger decision wait with a named approver until you add a tier.
How does it find AI tools and agents we did not register?

From sign-ins, OAuth grants, vendor usage reports, browser signals and spend. It records metadata only and never reads prompts or outputs. Each agent gets an owner, a risk tier and a re-attestation date.
How does it work with Jira or Azure DevOps?
It reads work items and dates to derive project status and, if you switch it on, creates epics in one project you name. It never edits tasks or plans.
Where is our data kept?
In your region. The EU and the US are available at launch, and the UK and Australia on request. You can export everything continuously to a bucket you own.
What happens if we want to leave?
Your data is already in your bucket in a documented schema, and we commit to a wind-down of at least 90 days.
Which features can I use today?

None of them are generally available yet. The status on each feature shows what opens first to design partners (Early access), what follows in the first full release (Soon), and what is Planned or Later. Talk to us and we will tell you where your needs fall.
